page: UpCloud GPU-24xCPU-480GB-2xH100 is a GPU-accelerated server configured with 24 vCPUs and 480 GB of system memory. The processing power is driven by an Intel Xeon 8462Y+ processor running at 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 24 physical cores with a single thread per core. This instance is equipped with two NVIDIA Hopper H100 GPUs, providing a combined 160 GB of high-bandwidth video memory. It operates on the KVM hypervisor. Notably, this configuration does not include local storage, meaning external storage solutions must be attached.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong memory and processing capabilities. The memory subsystem achieved a strong read-only small block bandwidth of 4086.55 GB/sec and a large block write bandwidth of 110.72 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression reached a top-tier throughput of 35.53 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression scored a strong 355.23 GB/sec. The Intel Xeon processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, contribute to a Passmark CPU extended instructions score of 68491.94. For AI workloads, the hardware achieved top-tier LLM inference performance on a small 135M model, processing prompts at 10457.59 tokens/sec and generating text at 366.07 tokens/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by pairing a massive 480 GB RAM footprint with dual enterprise-grade H100 GPUs, making it highly efficient for memory-intensive parallel computing. However, a key tradeoff is the shared CPU allocation, which may introduce performance variability compared to dedicated CPU instances. Additionally, the complete absence of local storage requires users to factor in the performance and cost of network-attached storage. This server is highly suited for deep learning, large language model inference, heavy data science pipelines, and high-throughput database operations.
